claims.text: Resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation in CoCrFeMnNi-based HEA/Mo multilayer coatings is primarily governed by a high density of coherent, abrupt HEA/Mo interfaces.
HEA/Mo interfaces block dislocation motion during creep.
The overall composition can be held constant while interface density is varied by controlling individual layer thickness.
Varying individual layer thickness from 5 to 50 nm and changing the number of layers will modulate interface density and character.
Numerous thin layers produce a higher interface density than fewer thick layers.
Interface density and coherence constitute the structural mediator governing deformation resistance.
Chemically and crystallographically abrupt interfaces interrupt and arrest dislocation motion.
Arresting dislocation motion limits dislocation pile-up.
Limiting dislocation pile-up reduces the accumulation of plastic strain during sustained loading and delays creep onset.
Coatings with thinner layers and higher interface density will have lower creep rate and lower time-dependent strain than coatings with thicker layers.
Coatings with thinner layers and higher interface density will have lower creep rate and lower time-dependent strain than monolithic HEA coatings.
Monolithic HEA coatings and multilayers with few, thick layers will show more pronounced creep deformation under otherwise identical conditions.
The proposed interface-controlled behavior applies at 300–500 °C and moderate stress levels.
Introducing Mo may create compositional effects that confound the geometric effect of interface density.
The hypothesis is most directly applicable when interfacial chemical contrasts are minimized or comparably controlled.
Chemically similar interface layers or compositional modulation within the HEA system could help separate interface-density effects from Mo-related chemical effects.
Failure of higher-interface-density samples to show a significant creep reduction, or observation of accelerated creep, would falsify interface-barrier control under the tested conditions.
